guardrail: Do not run paid model/API benchmark prompts without explicit approval of model, reps, task list, and budget.

candidates.name: Local synthetic coding benchmark
candidates.harness: pi RPC runner plus generated npm test project
pros: executable correctness after each coding turn
controlled context pressure via verbose briefings
cons: synthetic tasks do not measure public-benchmark generalization
small generated project may be easier than real repository work
candidates.recommendedUse: First non-free smoke test for pruner loading, cost, latency, context pressure, and coding-turn correctness.

candidates.name: SWE-bench Pro public
candidates.harness: Docker, Modal, or local Docker patch evaluation
cons: requires a separate pi patch-generation adapter
tasks vary in duration and context pressure
candidates.recommendedUse: Primary future benchmark after a baseline screen selects tasks where pruning or compaction actually occurs.

candidates.name: SWE-bench Verified
cons: many tasks may finish before pruning matters
Python-only subset is less representative for this pruner comparison
candidates.recommendedUse: Calibration/control set, not the primary pruning-effect score unless task traces cross context-pressure thresholds.

candidates.name: Terminal-Bench software-engineering subset
pros: public task harness with executable tests
cons: requires curation to avoid sysadmin/security/puzzle contamination
candidates.recommendedUse: Separate secondary stress track for terminal-heavy long-horizon behavior.
